title: CUET General Test Test 1
subject: General Test (Code: 501)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/General Test - 501.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: CUET (UG) 2025 and 2026 General Test shift analyses (no questions copied)

instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
The last 5 questions are a data-interpretation set based on one table; the set stays together.

questions.sub_topic: Position from the right end of a row
questions.question: In a row of 40 students facing north, Anu is 12th from the left end. Binu is 5th to the right of Anu. What is Binu's position from the right end?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 24th
Answer steps: Binu's position from the left = 12 + 5 = 17th. Position from the right = 40 − 17 + 1 = 24th.
Why not the others: (B) forgets to add 1. (C) adds 1 twice. (D) uses Anu's position instead of Binu's (40 − 12 = 28).
Key point: Position from right = total − position from left + 1.

questions.sub_topic: Square of x plus its reciprocal
questions.question: If x + 1/x = 5, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 23
Given: x + 1/x = 5.
Step 1: Square both sides: x² + 2·x·(1/x) + 1/x² = 25.
Step 2: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 25, so x² + 1/x² = 23.
Common mistake: squaring only the 5 (option A) and forgetting the middle term 2.

questions.sub_topic: Day of the week for 15 August 2025
questions.question: 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday. What day of the week was 15 August 2025?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Friday
Answer steps: days from 1 January to 15 August = 30 (rest of January) + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 15 = 226. 226 = 7 × 32 + 2, so 2 odd days. Wednesday + 2 = Friday.
Why not the others: (A) counts only 1 odd day (a slip in counting January). (B) counts 3 odd days, as if February had 29 days — but 2025 is not a leap year. (D) assumes the days divide exactly by 7.
Key point: Count the days after the given date, then use the remainder on division by 7.

questions.question: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 1973
Why: Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973, beginning with nine tiger reserves, including Jim Corbett.
Why not the others: (A) is the year of the Wildlife (Protection) Act. (C) and (D) are not linked to Project Tiger (Project Elephant began in 1992).
Key point: Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972; Project Tiger 1973; Project Elephant 1992.

questions.question: India won the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 by defeating which team in the final at Dubai on 9 March 2025?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) New Zealand
Why: India beat New Zealand by four wickets in the final in Dubai, winning the Champions Trophy for the third time (after 2002, shared, and 2013). Rohit Sharma was Player of the Match.
Why not the others: India beat Australia in the semi-final; South Africa and Pakistan did not reach the final.
Key point: Champions Trophy titles for India: 2002 (shared), 2013, 2025.

questions.sub_topic: Profit after marking up and discount
questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article 25% above its cost price and then allows a discount of 12% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 10%
Given: let cost price = 100.
Step 1: Marked price = 125.
Step 2: Selling price = 125 − 12% of 125 = 125 − 15 = 110.
Step 3: Profit = 10 on a cost of 100, so 10%.
Common mistake: subtracting the percentages directly (25 − 12 = 13%, option A); the discount is on the marked price, not on the cost.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha:
A. Its maximum strength is 250 members.
B. It is a permanent body and is not dissolved.
C. One-third of its members retire every second year.
D. A Money Bill can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A, B and D only
C) A, B and C only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) A, B and C only
Why: A is correct: up to 238 elected members and 12 nominated by the President (Article 80). B and C are correct: the Rajya Sabha is never dissolved, and one-third of its members retire every two years.
Why not the others: D is wrong: a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha (Article 109). Options (A) and (D) include D; (B) leaves out the correct statement A.
Key point: Money Bills begin in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha can only delay them for 14 days.

questions.question: Which of the following has a pH less than 7?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Lemon juice
Why: Lemon juice contains citric acid, so it is acidic (pH about 2–3).
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are basic, with pH above 7.
Key point: pH below 7 — acidic; 7 — neutral; above 7 — basic.

questions.sub_topic: Letter coding by shifting one place
questions.question: In a certain code, COLD is written as DPME. How is WARM written in that code?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) XBSN
Answer steps: each letter is moved one place forward — C→D, O→P, L→M, D→E. So W→X, A→B, R→S, M→N, giving XBSN.
Why not the others: (A) changes the order of the last two letters. (B) moves W two places. (D) moves every letter one place back.
Key point: Find the rule from every letter, not just the first.

questions.question: What is the distance between the points (2, 3) and (8, 11)?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 10 units
Given: points (2, 3) and (8, 11).
Step 1: Differences: 8 − 2 = 6 and 11 − 3 = 8.
Step 2: Distance = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 units.
Common mistake: adding the differences (6 + 8 = 14, option A) instead of using the distance formula.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A ship made of iron floats on water, though an iron nail sinks.
Reason (R): A floating body displaces a weight of water equal to its own weight, and the hollow shape of a ship lets it displace a large volume of water.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true. By Archimedes' principle, the upthrust equals the weight of water displaced. The hollow ship displaces enough water to balance its weight; a solid nail displaces only its own small volume, which weighs less than the nail, so it sinks. (R) explains (A).
Why not the others: (B) denies the link. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: Floating depends on the weight of water displaced, not on the material alone.

questions.sub_topic: Total surface area of a cylinder
questions.question: A closed cylinder has a radius of 7 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its total surface area? (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 748 cm²
Given: r = 7 cm, h = 10 cm.
Step 1: Total surface area = 2πr(r + h).
Step 2: = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × (7 + 10) = 44 × 17 = 748 cm².
Common mistake: giving only the curved surface (2πrh = 440 cm², option A), adding only one circular end (440 + 154 = 594 cm², option B), or giving the volume (1540 cm³, option D).

questions.question: The 30th UN Climate Change Conference (COP30) was held in November 2025 in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Belém, Brazil
Why: COP30 was held in Belém, in the Amazon region of Brazil, from 10 to 21 November 2025.
Why not the others: (B) hosted COP29 (2024). (C) hosted COP28 (2023). (D) hosted the 1992 Earth Summit, not COP30.
Key point: COP stands for the Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the changes to GST rates that came into effect on 22 September 2025:
A. Most goods and services now fall under two main slabs of 5% and 18%.
B. A special rate of 40% applies to a small number of sin and luxury goods.
C. The 12% and 28% slabs were kept for most goods.
D. The changes were approved at the 56th meeting of the GST Council.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) B, C and D only
D) A, B and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) A, B and D only
Why: The GST Council, at its 56th meeting on 3 September 2025, approved a two-slab structure of 5% and 18%, with a special 40% rate for a few sin and luxury goods. The new rates took effect on 22 September 2025.
Why not the others: C is wrong: most items in the 12% slab moved to 5%, and most items in the 28% slab moved to 18%. Options (A) and (B) include C; (C) leaves out the correct statement D.
Key point: The reform is often called "GST 2.0" (5% and 18%, plus 40% for sin goods).

questions.question:
Statements:
All roses are flowers.
Some flowers are red.
Conclusions:
I. Some roses are red.
II. All flowers are roses.
Which of the conclusions follow?
options: C) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Neither I nor II follows
Answer steps: The red flowers may or may not include roses, so "Some roses are red" is not certain. "All roses are flowers" does not mean that all flowers are roses. Neither conclusion is certain.
Why not the others: (A) assumes the red flowers must include roses. (B) reverses the first statement. (C) accepts both errors.
Key point: A conclusion follows only if it is true in every possible diagram.

questions.sub_topic: Rate at which RBI lends to banks
questions.question: The rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term money to commercial banks against government securities is called the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Repo rate
Why: Under a repurchase (repo) agreement, banks borrow from the RBI for a short period by selling securities that they agree to buy back.
Why not the others: (B) is the rate at which the RBI borrows from banks. (C) is the rate for longer-term loans to banks without such a repurchase agreement. (D) is the share of deposits banks must keep with the RBI, not a lending rate.
Key point: Repo — RBI lends; reverse repo — RBI borrows.

questions.sub_topic: Definite conclusion from an inequality chain
questions.question: If A > B, B ≥ C and C > D, which of the following is definitely true?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A > D
Answer steps: A > B ≥ C > D, so A is greater than D.
Why not the others: (B) and (D) contradict B ≥ C > D. (C) contradicts A > B ≥ C.
Key point: Join the inequalities into one chain and read the ends.

questions.question: Ravi walks 6 km north, turns right and walks 8 km, then turns right again and walks 6 km. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 8 km east
Answer steps: north 6 km; a right turn from north faces east, so 8 km east; a right turn from east faces south, so 6 km south. The north and south walks cancel, leaving him 8 km east of the start.
Why not the others: (A) turns left instead of right. (C) is his distance after only the first two walks (√(36 + 64) = 10). (D) adds all three distances.
Key point: Draw the path; equal walks in opposite directions cancel.

questions.question: Baking soda, used in cooking, has which chemical formula?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) NaHCO₃
Why: Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO₃. On heating it gives off carbon dioxide, which makes dough rise.
Why not the others: (A) is washing soda (sodium carbonate, as Na₂CO₃·10H₂O). (B) is caustic soda. (D) is limestone or chalk.
Key point: Baking soda — NaHCO₃; washing soda — Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

questions.sub_topic: Seating five friends in a row
questions.question: Five friends P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. R sits in the middle. P sits second to the left of R. Q sits to the immediate right of R. T does not sit at either end. Who sits at the right end?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) S
Answer steps: number the seats 1 to 5 from left to right. R is in seat 3. P is second to the left of R: seat 1. Q is to the immediate right of R: seat 4. T is not at an end, so T takes seat 2. S takes the remaining seat 5, the right end.
Why not the others: (A) Q is in seat 4. (C) T is in seat 2. (D) P is at the left end.
Key point: Fix the definite positions first, then fill in the rest.

questions.question: Three bells ring at intervals of 12, 15 and 20 minutes. If they ring together at 8:00 a.m., when will they next ring together?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 9:00 a.m.
Given: intervals 12, 15 and 20 minutes.
Step 1: LCM of 12, 15 and 20 = 2² × 3 × 5 = 60 minutes.
Step 2: 8:00 a.m. + 60 minutes = 9:00 a.m.
Common mistake: adding the intervals (12 + 15 + 20 = 47 minutes, option A) instead of taking their LCM.

questions.sub_topic: Work finished by B after A leaves
questions.question: A can finish a piece of work in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 3 days, and then A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 10.5 days
Given: A's rate = 1/12 of the work a day; B's rate = 1/18 a day.
Step 1: Together = 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36 a day.
Step 2: In 3 days they finish 15/36; the remaining work is 21/36.
Step 3: B alone needs (21/36) ÷ (1/18) = 21/36 × 18 = 10.5 days.
Common mistake: forgetting that A also worked for the first 3 days, or subtracting 3 from 18 (15 days).

questions.sub_topic: Articles of the Constitution and their subjects
questions.question:
Match the Articles of the Constitution of India in List-I with their subjects in List-II:

List-I
(A) Article 14
(B) Article 21
(C) Article 32
(D) Article 51A

List-II
(I) Right to constitutional remedies
(II) Fundamental Duties
(III) Equality before law
(IV) Protection of life and personal liberty
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Article 14 — equality before law (III); Article 21 — protection of life and personal liberty (IV); Article 32 — right to constitutional remedies, which Dr Ambedkar called the "heart and soul" of the Constitution (I); Article 51A — Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976 (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Articles 14 and 21; (C) swaps Articles 21 and 32; (D) swaps Articles 32 and 51A.
Key point: Fundamental Rights are in Part III (Articles 12–35); Fundamental Duties in Part IVA.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the ozone layer:
A. It is found mainly in the stratosphere.
B. It absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.
C. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) deplete it.
D. The Montreal Protocol is an agreement to cut emissions of carbon dioxide.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A, B and C only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A, B and C only
Why: A, B and C are correct: the ozone layer lies mainly in the stratosphere (about 15–35 km up), it absorbs UV-B and UV-C radiation, and chlorine from CFCs breaks down ozone.
Why not the others: D is wrong: the Montreal Protocol (1987) phases out ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs; carbon dioxide is dealt with under the climate treaties (the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement). Options (C) and (D) include D; (B) leaves out the correct statement B.
Key point: Montreal — ozone; Kyoto and Paris — climate.

questions.question: Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) School
Answer steps: a doctor works in a hospital; in the same way, a teacher works in a school.
Why not the others: (A) is the person a teacher teaches. (B) and (C) are things a teacher uses, not the workplace.
Key point: Identify the relation in the first pair (worker : workplace) and apply it exactly.

questions.question: The average of five numbers is 24. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining four numbers is 22. What is the number removed?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 32
Given: average of 5 numbers = 24; average of 4 numbers = 22.
Step 1: Sum of the 5 numbers = 5 × 24 = 120.
Step 2: Sum of the 4 numbers = 4 × 22 = 88.
Step 3: Number removed = 120 − 88 = 32.
Common mistake: subtracting the averages (24 − 22 = 2, option A).

questions.question:
Arrange the following organisms to form a food chain, starting with the producer:
A. Frog
B. Grass
C. Snake
D. Grasshopper
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) B, D, A, C
Why: Grass (producer) is eaten by the grasshopper (primary consumer), which is eaten by the frog (secondary consumer), which is eaten by the snake (tertiary consumer).
Why not the others: (A) has the frog eating grass. (B) begins with a consumer. (C) has the snake eaten by the frog.
Key point: A food chain begins with a green plant, the producer.

questions.sub_topic: Venn diagram of tea and coffee drinkers
questions.question: In a class of 60 students, 35 like tea, 30 like coffee and 10 like both. How many students like neither tea nor coffee?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 5
Answer steps: students who like at least one = 35 + 30 − 10 = 55. Those who like neither = 60 − 55 = 5.
Why not the others: (B) subtracts the "both" group twice. (C) adds 35 and 30 without removing the overlap and finds no one left. (D) confuses "neither" with "both".
Key point: n(A or B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(both).

questions.sub_topic: Statement and conclusion about festival buses
questions.question:
Statement: "During the festival, city buses will run every five minutes to reduce crowding at bus stops."
Conclusions:
I. Crowding at bus stops is expected during the festival.
II. Private vehicles will be banned during the festival.
Which of the conclusions follow?
options: B) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Only I follows
Answer steps: The buses are being increased "to reduce crowding", which assumes crowding is expected, so I follows. Nothing is said about private vehicles, so II does not follow.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) accept II, which brings in a new idea. (D) rejects I, which the statement implies.
Key point: A conclusion must follow from what is stated, not from what might also happen.

questions.question: Who wrote "Gitanjali", the collection of poems for which the Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded in 1913?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Rabindranath Tagore
Why: Rabindranath Tagore received the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature, the first awarded to an Asian, largely for the English "Gitanjali" (Song Offerings).
Why not the others: (A) wrote "Anandamath", which contains "Vande Mataram". (C) wrote "The Golden Threshold". (D) wrote "Godaan".
Key point: Tagore also wrote India's national anthem, "Jana Gana Mana".

questions.sub_topic: Assertion and reason on consecutive integers
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The product of any two consecutive integers is even.
Reason (R): The sum of any two consecutive integers is odd.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Answer steps: (A) is true: of two consecutive integers one is even, and a product with an even factor is even. (R) is also true: an even number plus an odd number is odd (e.g. 4 + 5 = 9). But the oddness of the sum does not explain why the product is even, so (R) is not the explanation of (A).
Why not the others: (A) treats a true but unrelated fact as the reason. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: Both statements can be true without one explaining the other.

questions.question: Force is measured in which SI unit?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Newton
Why: One newton is the force that gives a mass of 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m/s² (F = ma).
Why not the others: (B) is the unit of work and energy. (C) is the unit of power. (D) is the unit of pressure.
Key point: N = kg·m/s².

questions.sub_topic: Percentage less when one is 25% more
questions.question: A's salary is 25% more than B's salary. By what percentage is B's salary less than A's?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 20%
Given: let B = 100; then A = 125.
Step 1: Difference = 25.
Step 2: B is less than A by 25 ÷ 125 × 100 = 20%.
Common mistake: taking the difference on B's salary (25 ÷ 100 = 25%, option A); the base must be A, the salary we compare with.

questions.sub_topic: Nobel laureates of 2025 and their fields
questions.question:
Match the 2025 Nobel laureates in List-I with the field of their prize in List-II:

List-I
(A) María Corina Machado
(B) László Krasznahorkai
(C) Omar M. Yaghi (shared)
(D) John Clarke (shared)

List-II
(I) Literature
(II) Physics
(III) Peace
(IV) Chemistry
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: María Corina Machado of Venezuela — Peace, for her work for democratic rights (III); László Krasznahorkai of Hungary — Literature (I); Omar Yaghi, with Susumu Kitagawa and Richard Robson — Chemistry, for metal-organic frameworks (IV); John Clarke, with Michel Devoret and John Martinis — Physics, for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in an electric circuit (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Peace and Literature; (B) swaps Chemistry and Physics; (C) swaps Literature and Chemistry.
Key point: The 2025 Nobel Prizes were announced from 6 to 13 October 2025.

questions.sub_topic: Mission that took Shubhanshu Shukla to the ISS
questions.question: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla became the first Indian astronaut to visit the International Space Station in June 2025 as part of which mission?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Axiom-4 (Ax-4)
Why: Ax-4 was launched on 25 June 2025 from the Kennedy Space Center and docked with the ISS on 26 June 2025. Shukla spent about 18 days aboard.
Why not the others: (A) is the name of India's own human spaceflight programme, not the mission Shukla flew on. (B) is a planned lunar mission. (D) carried Rakesh Sharma, the first Indian in space, in 1984 — to the Salyut 7 station, not the ISS.
Key point: Rakesh Sharma (1984) — first Indian in space; Shubhanshu Shukla (2025) — first Indian on the ISS.

questions.sub_topic: State not crossed by the Tropic of Cancer
questions.question: Which one of the following states does the Tropic of Cancer NOT pass through?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Odisha
Why: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) passes through eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha lies wholly south of it.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are on the list of eight.
Key point: Learn the eight states from west to east.

questions.question:
Match the nutrients in List-I with the diseases caused by their deficiency in List-II:

List-I
(A) Vitamin C
(B) Vitamin D
(C) Iodine
(D) Vitamin A

List-II
(I) Goitre
(II) Night blindness
(III) Scurvy
(IV) Rickets
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Vitamin C — scurvy (bleeding gums) (III); Vitamin D — rickets (soft, bent bones) (IV); iodine — goitre (swollen thyroid) (I); Vitamin A — night blindness (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Vitamins C and D; (B) swaps iodine and Vitamin A; (D) swaps Vitamin D and iodine.
Key point: Iodised salt prevents goitre.

questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order (earliest first):
A. Gupta dynasty
B. Mughal dynasty
C. Maurya dynasty
D. Slave (Mamluk) dynasty of Delhi
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) C, A, D, B
Why: Maurya (from about 321 BCE), Gupta (from about 320 CE), the Slave dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate (from 1206 CE) and the Mughals (from 1526 CE, after the First Battle of Panipat).
Why not the others: (A) places the Delhi Sultanate before the Guptas. (C) places the Guptas before the Mauryas. (D) places the Mughals before the Delhi Sultanate.
Key point: Anchor dates help: 321 BCE, 320 CE, 1206, 1526.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Pacific Ocean
Why: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one-third of the Earth's surface.
Why not the others: (A) is the second largest. (B) is the third largest. (C) is the smallest.
Key point: Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic.

questions.sub_topic: Next term in a doubling series
questions.question: Find the next term in the series: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 127
Answer steps: each term is twice the previous term plus 1 — 3 × 2 + 1 = 7, 7 × 2 + 1 = 15, 15 × 2 + 1 = 31, 31 × 2 + 1 = 63, so 63 × 2 + 1 = 127.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) do not follow the rule. Note also that the differences (4, 8, 16, 32) double, giving 63 + 64 = 127.
Key point: Check both the differences and the ratio between terms.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922 after which incident?
options: C) The arrest of Bal Gangadhar Tilak
D) The failure of the Cripps Mission
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) The Chauri Chaura incident
Why: At Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur district, then United Provinces) in February 1922, a crowd set fire to a police station and policemen were killed. Gandhiji felt the movement had turned violent and called it off.
Why not the others: (B) happened in April 1919, before the movement began. (C) Tilak was not arrested at this time; he died in 1920. (D) The Cripps Mission came in 1942.
Key point: The Non-Cooperation Movement ran from 1920 to 1922.

questions.sub_topic: Part of the brain that controls balance
questions.question: Which part of the human brain maintains posture and balance of the body?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Cerebellum
Why: The cerebellum, at the back of the brain, coordinates voluntary movements and keeps posture and balance.
Why not the others: (A) controls thinking, memory and voluntary actions. (B) controls involuntary actions such as heartbeat and breathing. (C) controls body temperature, hunger and hormone release.
Key point: Cerebellum — balance; medulla — involuntary actions.

questions.question: A train 180 m long passes a pole in 12 seconds. How long will it take to cross a platform 270 m long at the same speed?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 30 seconds
Given: train length = 180 m; time to pass a pole = 12 s; platform = 270 m.
Step 1: Speed = 180 ÷ 12 = 15 m/s.
Step 2: To cross the platform, the train covers its own length plus the platform: 180 + 270 = 450 m.
Step 3: Time = 450 ÷ 15 = 30 s.
Common mistake: using only the platform length (270 ÷ 15 = 18 s, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Relation through only daughter of my mother
questions.question: Pointing to a boy, Riya said, "His mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is Riya related to the boy?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Mother
Answer steps: "The only daughter of my mother" is Riya herself (Riya is a woman speaking of her own mother). So the boy's mother is Riya.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) would need another daughter of Riya's mother. (C) is one generation too far.
Key point: "Only daughter of my mother", said by a woman, means the speaker herself.

questions.sub_topic: Time for a sum to become four times at simple interest
questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times itself at the same rate?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 24 years
Given: the sum doubles in 8 years, so the interest in 8 years = the principal (100%).
Step 1: Rate = 100% ÷ 8 = 12.5% a year.
Step 2: To become four times, the interest must be 300% of the principal.
Step 3: Time = 300 ÷ 12.5 = 24 years.
Common mistake: thinking that it doubles again in another 8 years (16 years, option B); that is true of compound interest, not simple interest.

questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Students enrolled in the five streams of a college

| Stream | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Arts | 240 | 300 |
| Science | 360 | 405 |
| Commerce | 300 | 330 |
| Vocational | 60 | 90 |
| Fine Arts | 40 | 75 |

Question: By what percentage did the total enrolment of the college increase from 2024 to 2025?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 20%
Given: total 2024 = 240 + 360 + 300 + 60 + 40 = 1000; total 2025 = 300 + 405 + 330 + 90 + 75 = 1200.
Step 1: Increase = 1200 − 1000 = 200.
Step 2: Percentage increase = 200 ÷ 1000 × 100 = 20%.
Common mistake: dividing by the new total (200 ÷ 1200 = 16.7%, option A) or giving the increase in students (200) as a percentage (option D).

questions.sub_topic: Stream with the highest percentage increase
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Students enrolled in the five streams of a college

| Stream | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Arts | 240 | 300 |
| Science | 360 | 405 |
| Commerce | 300 | 330 |
| Vocational | 60 | 90 |
| Fine Arts | 40 | 75 |

Question: Which stream recorded the highest percentage increase in enrolment from 2024 to 2025?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Fine Arts
Given: increases — Arts 60 on 240, Science 45 on 360, Commerce 30 on 300, Vocational 30 on 60, Fine Arts 35 on 40.
Step 1: Percentages — Arts 25%, Science 12.5%, Commerce 10%, Vocational 50%, Fine Arts 87.5%.
Step 2: The highest is Fine Arts (87.5%).
Common mistake: choosing Arts, which has the largest increase in numbers (60) but not in percentage.

questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Students enrolled in the five streams of a college

| Stream | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Arts | 240 | 300 |
| Science | 360 | 405 |
| Commerce | 300 | 330 |
| Vocational | 60 | 90 |
| Fine Arts | 40 | 75 |

Question: What percentage of the total enrolment in 2025 was in Science?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 33.75%
Given: Science 2025 = 405; total 2025 = 1200.
Step 1: 405 ÷ 1200 = 0.3375.
Step 2: As a percentage, 33.75%.
Common mistake: using the 2024 figures (360 ÷ 1000 = 36%, option B) or dividing 405 by 1000 (option D).

questions.sub_topic: Ratio of Arts to Commerce in 2025
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Students enrolled in the five streams of a college

| Stream | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Arts | 240 | 300 |
| Science | 360 | 405 |
| Commerce | 300 | 330 |
| Vocational | 60 | 90 |
| Fine Arts | 40 | 75 |

Question: What is the ratio of Arts students to Commerce students in 2025?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 10 : 11
Given: Arts 2025 = 300; Commerce 2025 = 330.
Step 1: 300 : 330.
Step 2: Divide both by 30: 10 : 11.
Common mistake: writing the ratio the wrong way round (11 : 10, option A), or using the 2024 Arts figure (240 : 330 = 8 : 11, option D).

questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Students enrolled in the five streams of a college

| Stream | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Arts | 240 | 300 |
| Science | 360 | 405 |
| Commerce | 300 | 330 |
| Vocational | 60 | 90 |
| Fine Arts | 40 | 75 |

Question: Suppose the total enrolment rises in 2026 by the same percentage as it did from 2024 to 2025, and Science keeps the same share of the total as in 2025. How many students will be enrolled in Science in 2026?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 486
Given: increase from 2024 to 2025 = 20%; Science share in 2025 = 33.75%.
Step 1: Total in 2026 = 1200 × 1.2 = 1440.
Step 2: Science = 33.75% of 1440 = 1440 × 0.3375 = 486.
Common mistake: applying the 2024 share of 36% to 1200 (432, option C), or adding 20% of the 2024 Science figure to 405 (405 + 72 = 477, option D).
